content: The Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) is regarded as the most reliable and definitive method for diagnosing Posttransplantation Diabetes Mellitus (PTDM). This test is generally conducted when the patient has achieved a stable condition under maintenance immunosuppressive therapy, which is typically around 45 days following the transplantation procedure. However, these methods are primarily utilized to identify individuals at higher risk of developing PTDM, allowing for closer observation and monitoring of these patients. In kidney transplant recipients, elevated pre-transplant levels of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) have been linked to an increased likelihood of developing PTDM. This suggests that hs-CRP could serve as a valuable early biomarker for assessing the risk of PTDM in this patient population.
